authz_enforced_server_side_centrally.title: Authorization Enforced Server-Side Centrally
authz_enforced_server_side_centrally.description: Attested true when access decisions are made server-side through a single reusable deny-by-default enforcement layer covering function-level and request-method (POST/PUT/DELETE) authorization, never trusting client-supplied role/flag values (cookies, hidden fields). False (client-side-only or scattered per-handler authz) fires broken access control — missing function-level authorization (CWE-862/863) — and metadata-tampering privilege escalation.

object_level_authz_ownership_enforced.title: Object-Level Authorization Ownership Enforced
object_level_authz_ownership_enforced.description: Attested true when every record access verifies the authenticated principal owns / is entitled to the specific object id (queries scoped by subject, e.g. WHERE owner_id = :current_user), never accepting a user-controlled key as proof of authorization. False fires IDOR/BOLA (CWE-639) — one principal reading/modifying another's records by id.

authn_enforced_on_every_endpoint.title: Authentication Enforced On Every Endpoint
authn_enforced_on_every_endpoint.description: Attested true when every non-public route requires an authenticated principal before business logic runs, with default-deny on unmatched/protected routes (global filter / per-route guard) and an explicit small public allowlist. False (ad-hoc per-handler auth with gaps) lets privileged routes be reached by forced-browsing without a session/token.

access_control_failures_logged_and_alert.title: Access-Control Failures Logged And Alerted
access_control_failures_logged_and_alert.description: Attested true when repeated access-control / authorization failures (403/authz-denied) are emitted to the log/SIEM and trigger alerting on anomalous volume. False fires the detectability gap — automated abuse such as forced browsing and IDOR/BOLA scanning goes unobserved.

bindable_field_allowlist_enforced.title: Bindable-Field Allowlist Enforced
bindable_field_allowlist_enforced.description: Attests that HTTP request parameters are bound onto domain objects through an explicit bindable-field allow-list / strong-parameters / DTO layer, so privileged fields (isAdmin/role) cannot be over-posted (mass assignment). Secure=true; the exposure fires when false (whole request body bound wholesale to a privilege-bearing entity).

jwt_signature_verified.title: JWT Signature Verified
jwt_signature_verified.description: The service cryptographically verifies the JWT signature against a server-pinned expected algorithm and key (not the token-declared header alg), and validates exp/iss/aud — so a caller cannot forge or tamper token (including role) claims. When false, forged/unverified/tampered tokens are trusted, enabling token-forgery privilege escalation and authentication bypass. Insecure value: false.

accepts_alg_none.title: Accepts alg=none Tokens
accepts_alg_none.description: The token verifier accepts the unsecured 'alg':'none' JWT (no signature) as valid. Interpreted from the verifier configuration; true means unsigned tokens are honored, enabling trivial token forgery. Insecure value: true.

rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible.title: RS256-to-HS256 Confusion Possible
rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible.description: The verifier trusts the token-declared algorithm and would accept an HS256-signed token verified against the RSA public key (RS256->HS256 key-confusion). Interpreted boolean; true means an attacker can forge tokens using the public key as an HMAC secret. Insecure value: true.

cookie_secure_flag.title: Session Cookie Secure Flag Set
cookie_secure_flag.description: Session cookies are issued with the Secure attribute so they are only transmitted over TLS. When false, the session cookie can leak over cleartext and be hijacked. Insecure value: false.

cookie_httponly_flag.title: Session Cookie HttpOnly Flag Set
cookie_httponly_flag.description: Session cookies are issued with the HttpOnly attribute so they are inaccessible to client-side script. When false, XSS can exfiltrate the session cookie. Insecure value: false.

samesite_attribute_set.title: Session Cookie SameSite Attribute Set
samesite_attribute_set.description: Session cookies set a SameSite attribute (Strict/Lax, and Secure when None) to constrain cross-site transmission. When false, the cookie is exposed to cross-site request contexts. Insecure value: false.

session_id_regenerated_on_auth.title: Session ID Regenerated On Authentication
session_id_regenerated_on_auth.description: The session identifier is regenerated on authentication and on privilege change. When false, a pre-authentication session id persists, enabling session fixation. Insecure value: false.

server_side_revocation_supported.title: Server-Side Session/Token Revocation Supported
server_side_revocation_supported.description: Sessions / JWTs can be invalidated server-side on logout or compromise (server-side session store or short-lived-plus-revocable tokens). When false, issued tokens/sessions remain valid until expiry and cannot be killed on logout. Insecure value: false.

parameterized_queries_used.title: Parameterized Queries Used
parameterized_queries_used.description: Interpreted attestation: all data-store access uses parameterized/prepared statements or safe ORM bindings. Secure value true. Fires the injection exposure (is_false) when query construction is NOT consistently parameterized — the primary A03:2021 SQLi/NoSQLi defect.

dynamic_query_string_concatenation.title: Dynamic Query-String Concatenation Used
dynamic_query_string_concatenation.description: Interpreted attestation: user-controlled input is concatenated/interpolated into query strings (raw SQL/NoSQL/LDAP filter construction with request data). Secure value false. Fires the injection exposure (is_true) — the direct SQLi/NoSQLi/LDAP-injection sink that parameterization eliminates.

user_input_in_shell_command_string.title: User Input In Shell Command String
user_input_in_shell_command_string.description: Interpreted attestation: user data is embedded into an OS shell command string (Runtime.exec(string), subprocess shell=True, child_process.exec). Secure value false. Fires the injection exposure (is_true) — the OS-command-injection sink.

os_commands_avoided_or_arg_array_used.title: OS Commands Avoided Or Arg-Array Used
os_commands_avoided_or_arg_array_used.description: Interpreted attestation: OS command execution is avoided in favour of native libraries, or where unavoidable the argument-array form is used so user data never becomes part of a shell string. Secure value true. Fires (is_false) when commands are built as shell strings — the OS-command-injection defect.

server_side_allowlist_validation.title: Server-Side Allowlist Validation Applied
server_side_allowlist_validation.description: Interpreted attestation: untrusted input is validated server-side at the trust boundary with allow-lists (type, length, charset, range). Secure value true. Fires (is_false) when no server-side allow-list validation gates input feeding queries/commands.

validation_is_client_side_only.title: Validation Is Client-Side Only
validation_is_client_side_only.description: Interpreted attestation: input validation is performed only client-side (UI) and not re-enforced server-side, so an attacker bypassing the UI submits unvalidated input. Secure value false. Fires (is_true) — client-only validation provides no real boundary protection against injection.

denylist_filtering_used.title: Denylist Filtering Used
denylist_filtering_used.description: Interpreted attestation: input is filtered with deny-lists / blacklist-of-bad-characters rather than allow-lists. Secure value false. Fires (is_true) — deny-list filtering is bypassable (encoding, alternate syntax) and is the insecure A03:2021 input-handling pattern.

outbound_fetch_destination_allowlisted.title: Outbound-Fetch Destination Allowlisted
outbound_fetch_destination_allowlisted.description: True when the service validates user-influenced outbound fetch destinations against an allow-list of hosts/schemes/ports (post-DNS-resolution) before issuing the request. False means the user-supplied URL is passed straight to the HTTP client, allowing SSRF to internal services.

private_and_metadata_targets_blocked.title: Private/Metadata Targets Blocked
private_and_metadata_targets_blocked.description: True when the service rejects outbound fetches resolving to RFC1918 private ranges, loopback (127.0.0.0/8), and link-local (169.254.0.0/16) after DNS resolution (defeating DNS-rebinding/redirect-to-internal). False permits SSRF pivots into the internal network and link-local services.

cloud_metadata_endpoint_blocked.title: Cloud Metadata Endpoint Blocked
cloud_metadata_endpoint_blocked.description: True when outbound fetches to the cloud instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254, and equivalents such as fd00:ec2::254) are explicitly blocked so user-influenced requests cannot harvest workload IAM credentials. False allows credential theft via the metadata API (ATT&CK T1552.005).

native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data.title: Native Deserialization Of Untrusted Data
native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data.description: Interpreted: the service natively deserializes attacker-controlled bytes (Java ObjectInputStream.readObject, Python pickle.load, PyYAML yaml.load without SafeLoader, Ruby Marshal.load, PHP unserialize) on untrusted input. True = insecure: such a deserialization sink on untrusted data triggers gadget chains leading to RCE. False = secure: untrusted data flows only through pure-data parsers (JSON / yaml.safe_load).

deserialization_class_allowlist_or_signe.title: Deserialization Class Allowlist Or Signed Payloads
deserialization_class_allowlist_or_signe.description: Interpreted: where serialized objects are unavoidable, payloads are integrity-protected (HMAC/signature verified before deserializing) AND deserialization is type-constrained to a strict class allow-list (look-ahead/resolveClass filter, ObjectInputFilter, SafeConstructor). True = secure: a tampered or unexpected-type payload is rejected before any gadget can be constructed. False = insecure: deserialization is unauthenticated and unconstrained.

contextual_output_encoding_applied.title: Contextual Output Encoding Applied
contextual_output_encoding_applied.description: Whether untrusted data is contextually output-encoded via framework auto-escaping (HTML/attribute/JS/URL context) before rendering. Secure when true. When false, reflected/stored/DOM XSS executes attacker script in victim browsers.

unsafe_html_sinks_used.title: Unsafe HTML Sinks Used
unsafe_html_sinks_used.description: Whether raw-HTML escape-hatches that bypass auto-escaping are present and fed untrusted data (e.g. dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML=, v-html, bypassSecurityTrust, Jinja |safe, render_template_string). Secure when false. Fires (is_true) when an XSS injection sink is in use.

content_security_policy_enforced.title: Content-Security-Policy Enforced
content_security_policy_enforced.description: Whether the service emits an enforcing Content-Security-Policy response header (e.g. default-src 'self') as defense-in-depth against script injection. Secure when true; when false there is no CSP backstop limiting injected-script execution.

csp_allows_unsafe_inline_or_eval.title: CSP Allows unsafe-inline Or unsafe-eval
csp_allows_unsafe_inline_or_eval.description: Whether the deployed CSP weakens script protection by permitting 'unsafe-inline' and/or 'unsafe-eval' script sources, which nullifies CSP's XSS mitigation. Secure when false. Fires (is_true) when the policy admits inline/eval script.

secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac.title: Secrets Hardcoded In Config Or IaC
secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac.description: Interpreted boolean: true when credentials/keys are baked into source/config files or IaC templates (Terraform/Helm/Compose) rather than pulled from a secret manager and injected at runtime. Fires the exposure when true — hardcoded secrets are harvested from the repo/artifact and reused against downstream stores (OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet).

least_privilege_service_identity.title: Least-Privilege Service Identity
least_privilege_service_identity.description: Whether the workload identity and downstream credentials are least-privilege and scoped per workload (scoped_per_workload, secure) versus a shared superuser/root/standing-admin credential reused across services (shared_admin_or_root, insecure). A shared admin identity turns any foothold into broad downstream compromise.

downstream_tls_enforced_and_validated.title: Downstream TLS Enforced And Validated
downstream_tls_enforced_and_validated.description: Whether calls to data stores and downstream services use TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation (tls_validated, secure) versus cleartext or insecure_skip_verify / rejectUnauthorized:false / sslmode=disable (plaintext_or_skip_verify, insecure). Cleartext or skip-verify downstream TLS lets harvested or in-flight credentials be intercepted, compounding the secrets exposure.

debug_and_verbose_errors_disabled_in_pro.title: Debug And Verbose Errors Disabled In Prod
debug_and_verbose_errors_disabled_in_pro.description: Attests that production returns generic error responses with debug mode off — stack traces, framework debug pages, and detailed internal messages (paths, queries, versions) are not exposed to clients. Insecure (false) when verbose errors or a debug console are reachable in production, leaking internals that aid further attack (A05:2021).

default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Accounts Removed Or Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: Attests that all default/sample accounts and default passwords shipped with the platform, framework, or appliance have been removed or had their credentials changed. Insecure (false) when any default account/password remains, giving attackers a trivial compromise path (A05:2021).

unnecessary_services_disabled.title: Unnecessary Services Disabled
unnecessary_services_disabled.description: Attests that unnecessary features, sample applications, admin consoles, debug endpoints, unused ports, and superfluous services are disabled or removed, minimizing the attack surface. Insecure (false) when sample apps / unused features / exposed admin consoles remain enabled (A05:2021).

hardened_baseline_documented.title: Hardened Baseline Documented
hardened_baseline_documented.description: Attests that the service configuration follows a documented, reviewed, version-controlled secure baseline (NIST CM-2/CM-6), so hardening is repeatable and drift is detectable. Insecure (false) when configuration is ad hoc / undocumented / not version-controlled, allowing silent misconfiguration drift (A05:2021).

dependency_vulnerability_scanning_enable.title: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning Enabled
dependency_vulnerability_scanning_enable.description: Attests that Software Composition Analysis (SCA) runs continuously in CI against all direct and nested dependencies, producing a current component inventory checked against CVE/NVD (e.g. osv-scanner, npm audit, OWASP Dependency-Check, retire.js, pip-audit). Insecure (false) when dependency versions are un-inventoried and no automated vulnerability scanning is in place (A06:2021).

known_vulnerable_dependencies_present.title: Known-Vulnerable Dependencies Present
known_vulnerable_dependencies_present.description: Interpreted finding: true when one or more direct or nested dependencies (OS packages, runtimes, libraries, app/web server, DBMS, APIs) are known-vulnerable, unsupported, or out-of-date with unremediated CVEs, or are unmaintained. Fires on true — each is a ready exploit path (A06:2021, CWE-1035/CWE-1104).

artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_.title: Artifact Supply-Chain Signed Provenance Verified
artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_.description: Attests that deployed artifacts/images are obtained from official sources over secure (TLS) links and their signatures/provenance (SLSA in-toto / cosign / signed packages) are verified against a pinned identity before deployment. Insecure (false) when artifacts are pulled unsigned/unverified, permitting malicious substitution (A06:2021, SLSA v1.0).
